summary: GRAVEYARD adversarial pass challenged all 12 active-batch theses independently. No thesis is outright falsified, but several hidden failure paths remain material: RKLB capital/integration load, CRDO/ARM/AVGO/ANET customer concentration, ALAB customer-linked warrant economics, NVDA/AMD/ASML export-policy sensitivity, TSM overseas-cost/geopolitical tradeoff, MU cycle-peak/capex risk, and VRT backlog conversion/cancellation quality. The batch is also highly exposed to one common failure regime: hyperscaler AI capex slows while custom silicon, export restrictions or project delays rise. Lane acquisition is complete for the requested graveyard falsification pass, but every company remains not ready_for_chief for T0 because unresolved underwriting blockers persist outside this lane.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Rocket Lab is simultaneously funding a launch-vehicle step-up and acquisition expansion. Strong backlog can still fail to translate if Neutron slips, integration absorbs cash, or financing/dilution rises.
contradictions: Mission cadence and backlog validate demand, but they do not prove medium-launch economics or acquisition integration quality.
unknowns: Post-acquisition liquidity bridge, exact Neutron cash need, backlog cancellation/termination mix.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Neutron qualification stays on schedule, acquisition integration is cash-manageable, and backlog converts with stable margins and no material financing surprise.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Concentration is the primary fragility. Rapid growth from a few hyperscaler programs can reverse quickly if architecture, procurement, or insourcing changes.
contradictions: High growth and profitability lower solvency risk but amplify expectations and dependence on continued program wins.
unknowns: End-customer mapping behind channel partners, contract duration, pricing protection and hyperscaler insourcing risk.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Revenue broadens across independent end customers while gross margin and growth remain durable after concentration declines.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: The Amazon performance warrant demonstrates strategic demand but creates customer-linked dilution/contra-revenue economics and may signal unusually high bargaining power by a major buyer.
contradictions: Profitability and growth support operating quality while a large customer can earn significant equity through purchasing milestones.
unknowns: Future vesting cadence, true customer concentration and economics net of warrant contra-revenue.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Non-Amazon customers diversify revenue fast enough that warrant-linked demand is not the dominant incremental driver.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Export controls can produce both immediate lost TAM and a longer-run substitute ecosystem. NVIDIA's moat can weaken even if global reported growth remains high if restricted markets accelerate local alternatives and cloud titans internalize silicon.
contradictions: Software/ecosystem leadership is exceptional, but policy and buyer power are external constraints.
unknowns: Custom-accelerator wallet share, duration of China exclusion and margin impact of increasingly system-level competition.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: NVIDIA sustains software lock-in, restores compliant strategic-market access and keeps custom-silicon share losses immaterial.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Strong Data Center growth can still mask accelerator-specific dependence on a small number of deployments and software ecosystem gaps versus NVIDIA; export constraints add inventory/TAM risk.
contradictions: EPYC strength is proven, while durable MI-series economics and repeat-scale breadth are less mature.
unknowns: MI buyer concentration, normalized accelerator gross margin and repeat-deployment breadth.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: MI-series scales across multiple production customers with sustained margin and increasing software stickiness.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Top-five end customers represented about 45% of revenue in the cited quarter and one distributor represented 42% of direct semiconductor sales. Custom AI success can therefore deepen customer bargaining power even as revenue rises.
contradictions: Broadcom's FCF and diversified franchises buffer financial stress but not custom-program concentration.
unknowns: AI program concentration by end customer, customer switching rights and VMware integration/tax-indemnity tail risk.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AI growth broadens across programs/customers while top-customer share falls and deleveraging continues without integration erosion.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: TSMC's geographic diversification is not free. Management expects multi-year overseas-fab margin dilution, while Taiwan remains the core advanced-node concentration. A geopolitical shock and higher structural cost can coexist.
contradictions: Overseas fabs improve resilience but can reduce margin advantage and capital efficiency.
unknowns: Customer willingness to absorb resilience premium, overseas yield convergence and customer concentration at advanced nodes.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Overseas economics converge faster than guided while advanced-node leadership and customer diversity remain intact.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Near-monopoly equipment economics are exposed to export controls, customer capex cyclicality and critical suppliers. China represented 29.1% of 2025 net sales, making policy a direct operating variable.
contradictions: Scarcity pricing power is strong while political access to end markets can change abruptly.
unknowns: Quantified critical-supplier concentration, 2026 China mix and High-NA customer ROI at full production scale.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Restrictions expand without material order loss, High-NA economics meet customer thresholds and supplier redundancy improves.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Top five customers represented 57% of FY2026 revenue, Arm China alone 16%, and related-party revenue rose sharply. SoftBank/control and customer concentration can undermine the apparent resilience of the royalty model; RISC-V remains a credible substitute.
contradictions: Royalty scalability is excellent while governance/commercial concentration remains unusually high.
unknowns: AGI CPU economics, Arm China durability, related-party dependence and RISC-V substitution in new workloads.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: External royalty growth broadens materially, related-party share normalizes and RISC-V displacement remains contained.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Current HBM scarcity and profitability can attract supply while Micron commits to a very large U.S. fab program. Low valuation on peak earnings is a classic memory-cycle trap if pricing mean reverts before new capacity earns returns.
contradictions: Long-term AI memory demand is strong while memory economics remain supply-responsive and capital intensive.
unknowns: HBM4 competitor yield/volume, contract floors and normalized free-cash-flow after elevated capex.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: HBM pricing/mix and margins remain resilient through capacity additions without leverage or FCF deterioration.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Historically meaningful Microsoft/Meta concentration makes Arista vulnerable to a small number of cloud architecture decisions. Internal/proprietary fabrics, custom networking and white-box alternatives can cap share even with excellent execution.
contradictions: Customer satisfaction and product innovation are strong, yet cloud titans can alter architecture and procurement rapidly.
unknowns: Current top-customer share, white-box substitution rate and 1.6T/XPO buyer breadth.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Customer share diversifies while Arista wins multiple new large AI-fabric deployments against internal/white-box alternatives.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: A $15B backlog can overstate realized economics because filings explicitly allow cancellations/rescheduling and acquired businesses may have differing termination rights. Power/interconnection constraints can delay customer projects even when Vertiv demand is genuine.
contradictions: Order growth validates demand while conversion timing/quality can still disappoint.
unknowns: Backlog aging, customer concentration, cancellation/reschedule rates and margin by backlog vintage.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Backlog converts on schedule with stable margins, low cancellations and broad customer mix through multiple quarters.

materialFindings.finding: Customer concentration is not a niche issue in this batch: CRDO, ARM, AVGO and ANET all have direct or historical evidence that a small number of large buyers can materially swing outcomes.
Policy can create substitution, not merely near-term revenue loss: NVIDIA and ASML face export-control exposure that can accelerate alternative ecosystems and local supply chains.

Batch diversification is overstated by ticker count because most names depend on the same AI-capex/power-buildout regime; a synchronized hyperscaler capex reset is the highest-value common pre-mortem.

contradictions: Strong balance sheets and growth do not eliminate customer/policy/common-shock fragility.
Resilience investments can reduce geopolitical risk while worsening cost and capital intensity.
Backlog/order strength is not equivalent to realized revenue quality.
unknowns: Comparable current end-customer concentration is not normalized across every batch company.
Current market-implied expectations are intentionally left to expectations-execution and not used here.
Several companies still lack quantified cancellation, contract-duration or customer-insourcing evidence.

peerRequests.request: Close the remaining comparable concentration/backlog/share-count blockers before any ready_for_chief promotion, especially CRDO, ARM, ALAB, RKLB and VRT.
Run a common-shock AI-capex downshift and export-control substitution scenario across the batch rather than treating names as independent.

accuracyDebates.reason: Most active-batch names depend on overlapping hyperscaler AI spending and therefore are less diversified than ticker count suggests.
ALAB's purchase-vesting warrant is decision-relevant evidence of both validation and buyer leverage.
